ev.q: Compared with whites, AI/AN had significantly higher prevalences of sugar-sweetened beverage consumption (33.0% versus 26.8%)
AI/AN also reported a lower prevalence of having a personal doctor or health care provider (63.1%) than did whites (72.8%).
The prevalence of having health care coverage was higher among AI/AN (74.1%)
Group differences were assessed with pairwise tests (AI/AN versus whites and AI/AN versus others) with statistical significance defined as p<0.05.
Age-adjusted prevalences standardized to the projected 2000 U.S. population
because this is a cross-sectional study, causality cannot be inferred.
